businesses.business: senior housing and skilled nursing real estate

offering_description.value: LTC Properties owns and leases senior housing and skilled nursing facilities to care providers. It finances properties for owners and operators and hires third-party managers to run some of its senior housing communities.

primary_services.value: facility leasing; commercial mortgage and mezzanine lending; senior housing and resident care

customer_segment.value: B2B: senior living operators, skilled nursing providers, and healthcare property owners; B2C: older adults living in company-owned communities run by third-party managers

end_markets.value: senior living, including assisted living and memory care; skilled nursing and rehabilitation

revenue_model.value: rental or leasing: rent from operators under long-term facility leases; interest or premiums: interest on mortgages and other loans to property owners and operators; service fees: housing and care fees paid by residents at managed communities
revenue_model.category: rental or leasing; interest or premiums; service fees

value_chain_position.value: asset operator: acquires facilities and leases them to care providers or hires managers to serve residents; financial intermediary: provides property-backed financing to senior housing and skilled nursing owners and operators

geography_served.value: US national: properties and loans across multiple U.S. regions

specialization.value: related lines: senior housing and skilled nursing property leasing, property financing, and managed senior housing

distribution_channels.value: direct sales: directly negotiated leases and loans with property owners and care operators; partners / resellers: third-party senior living managers that market communities and enroll residents

regulatory_exposure.value: medium: federal REIT tax rules and state licensing and safety standards for care facilities

notes: The current balance among leased properties, financing, and managed senior housing is uncertain.
